#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

using db = double;
using ll = long long;
using ld = long double;
using ui = unsigned int;
using ull = unsigned long long;

using pdd = pair<db, db>;
using pdl = pair<db, ld>;
using pld = pair<ld, db>;
using ldp = pair<ld, ld>;

using pll = pair<ll, ll>;
using pil = pair<int, ll>;
using pli = pair<ll, int>;
using pii = pair<int, int>;

#define f first
#define s second
#define en end()
#define bg begin()
#define rev reverse
#define mp make_pair
#define pb push_back

#define y1 y1234567890
#define um unordered_map

#define all(x) x.bg, x.en
#define sz(x) (int)x.size()
#define len(x) (int)strlen(x)

#define sqr(x) ((x + 0ll) * (x))
#define sqrd(x) ((x + 0.0) * (x))

#define forn(i, n) for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)

const ll inf = (ll)1e18;
const ll mod = (ll)1e9 + 7;

const db eps = (db)1e-9;
const db pi = acos(-1.0);

const int dx[] = {0, 0, 1, 0, -1};
const int dy[] = {0, 1, 0, -1, 0};

const int N = (1 << 20);

ll bp(ll x, ll y){
    ll z = 1;
    while(y){
        if(y & 1)
            z = z * x % mod;
        x = x * x % mod;
        y >>= 1;    
    }
    return z;
}

ll ans, n, p[6][6], F[N], nump, m[N];
vector <pair <int, int> > E;

int main() {
    ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    
    cin >> n;
    for(int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j){
            cin >> p[i][j];
            p[i][j] = p[i][j] * bp(100, mod - 2) % mod; 
        }
    
    for(int i = n; i < 6; ++i)
        for(int j = n; j < 6; ++j)
            p[i][j] = 1;
    
    for(int i = 0; i < 6; ++i)
        for(int j = 0; j < 3; ++j)
            E.emplace_back(i, j);

    for(int i = 0; i < 6; ++i)
        for(int j = i + 1; j < 6; ++j)
            for(int k = j + 1; k < 6; ++k){
                vector <int> v;
                v.pb(i);
                v.pb(j);
                v.pb(k);
                do{
                    int mask1 = ((1 << (v[0] * 3)) ^ (1 << (v[1] * 3 + 1)) ^ (1 << (v[2] * 3 + 2)));
                    for(int mask = 0; mask < (1 << 18); ++mask)
                        if((mask & mask1) == mask1)
                            m[mask] |= (1 << nump);
                }while(next_permutation(v.begin(), v.end()));    
                nump++;
            }        

    for(int mask = 0; mask < (1 << 18); ++mask){
        ll v = 1;
        for(int i = 0; i < 18; ++i){
            if((mask >> i) & 1)
                v = v * p[E[i].f][E[i].s] % mod;
            else v = v * ((1 - p[E[i].f][E[i].s] + mod) % mod) % mod;
        }
        F[m[mask]] += v;
        if(F[m[mask]] >= mod)
            F[m[mask]] -= mod;
    }

    for(int i = 0; i < 20; ++i)
        for(int mask = 0; mask < (1 << 20); ++mask)
            if(mask & (1<<i))
                F[mask] = (F[mask] + F[mask ^ (1 << i)]) % mod;

    for(int i = 0; i < (1 << 18); ++i)
        m[i] = 0;

    nump = 0;

    for(int i = 0; i < 6; ++i)
        for(int j = i + 1; j < 6; ++j)
            for(int k = j + 1; k < 6; ++k){
                vector <int> v;
                for(int ii = 0; ii < 6; ++ii)
                    if(ii != i && ii != j && ii != k)
                        v.pb(ii);
                do{
                    int mask1 = ((1 << (v[0] * 3)) ^ (1 << (v[1] * 3 + 1)) ^ (1 << (v[2] * 3 + 2)));
                    for(int mask = 0; mask < (1 << 18); ++mask)
                        if((mask & mask1) == mask1)
                            m[mask] |= (1 << nump);
                }while(next_permutation(v.begin(), v.end()));    
                nump++;
            }

    E.clear();
    for(int i = 0; i < 6; ++i)
        for(int j = 3; j < 6; ++j)
            E.emplace_back(i, j);

    for(int mask = 0; mask < (1 << 18); ++mask){
        ll v = 1;
        for(int i = 0; i < 18; ++i){
            if((mask >> i) & 1)
                v = v * p[E[i].f][E[i].s] % mod;
            else v = v * ((1 - p[E[i].f][E[i].s] + mod) % mod) % mod;
        }
        ans = (ans + v * ((1 - F[((1 << 20) - 1) ^ m[mask]]  + mod) % mod) % mod) % mod; 
    }
    
    cout << ans << '\n';
    
    return 0;
}

problem_description.description: This is an easier version of the problem. In this version, $$$n \le 6$$$.Marek is working hard on creating strong testcases to his new algorithmic problem. You want to know what it is? Nah, we're not telling you. However, we can tell you how he generates the testcases.Marek chooses an integer $$$n$$$ and $$$n^2$$$ integers $$$p_{ij}$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le n$$$). He then generates a random bipartite graph with $$$2n$$$ vertices. There are $$$n$$$ vertices on the left side: $$$\ell_1, \ell_2, \dots, \ell_n$$$, and $$$n$$$ vertices on the right side: $$$r_1, r_2, \dots, r_n$$$. For each $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$, he puts an edge between vertices $$$\ell_i$$$ and $$$r_j$$$ with probability $$$p_{ij}$$$ percent.It turns out that the tests will be strong only if a perfect matching exists in the generated graph. What is the probability that this will occur?It can be shown that this value can be represented as $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are coprime integers and $$$Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Let $$$Q^{-1}$$$ be an integer for which $$$Q \cdot Q^{-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Print the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{-1}$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$\mathbf{1 \le n \le 6}$$$). The following $$$n$$$ lines describe the probabilities of each edge appearing in the graph. The $$$i$$$-th of the lines contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_{i1}, p_{i2}, \dots, p_{in}$$$ ($$$0 \le p_{ij} \le 100$$$); $$$p_{ij}$$$ denotes the probability, in percent, of an edge appearing between $$$\ell_i$$$ and $$$r_j$$$.
problem_description.output_spec: Print a single integer — the probability that the perfect matching exists in the bipartite graph, written as $$$P \cdot Q^{-1} \pmod{10^9+7}$$$ for $$$P$$$, $$$Q$$$ defined above.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample test, each of the $$$16$$$ graphs below is equally probable. Out of these, $$$7$$$ have a perfect matching:  Therefore, the probability is equal to $$$\frac{7}{16}$$$. As $$$16 \cdot 562\,500\,004 = 1 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$, the answer to the testcase is $$$7 \cdot 562\,500\,004 \mod{(10^9+7)} = 937\,500\,007$$$.

problem_description.description: This is an easier version of the problem. In this version, $$$n \le 6$$$.Marek is working hard on creating strong testcases to his new algorithmic problem. You want to know what it is? Nah, we're not telling you. However, we can tell you how he generates the testcases.Marek chooses an integer $$$n$$$ and $$$n^2$$$ integers $$$p_{ij}$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le n$$$). He then generates a random bipartite graph with $$$2n$$$ vertices. There are $$$n$$$ vertices on the left side: $$$\ell_1, \ell_2, \dots, \ell_n$$$, and $$$n$$$ vertices on the right side: $$$r_1, r_2, \dots, r_n$$$. For each $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$, he puts an edge between vertices $$$\ell_i$$$ and $$$r_j$$$ with probability $$$p_{ij}$$$ percent.It turns out that the tests will be strong only if a perfect matching exists in the generated graph. What is the probability that this will occur?It can be shown that this value can be represented as $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are coprime integers and $$$Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Let $$$Q^{-1}$$$ be an integer for which $$$Q \cdot Q^{-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Print the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{-1}$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$\mathbf{1 \le n \le 6}$$$). The following $$$n$$$ lines describe the probabilities of each edge appearing in the graph. The $$$i$$$-th of the lines contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_{i1}, p_{i2}, \dots, p_{in}$$$ ($$$0 \le p_{ij} \le 100$$$); $$$p_{ij}$$$ denotes the probability, in percent, of an edge appearing between $$$\ell_i$$$ and $$$r_j$$$.
problem_description.output_spec: Print a single integer — the probability that the perfect matching exists in the bipartite graph, written as $$$P \cdot Q^{-1} \pmod{10^9+7}$$$ for $$$P$$$, $$$Q$$$ defined above.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample test, each of the $$$16$$$ graphs below is equally probable. Out of these, $$$7$$$ have a perfect matching:  Therefore, the probability is equal to $$$\frac{7}{16}$$$. As $$$16 \cdot 562\,500\,004 = 1 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$, the answer to the testcase is $$$7 \cdot 562\,500\,004 \mod{(10^9+7)} = 937\,500\,007$$$.

}

    base %= MOD;
    while (exp) {
        if (exp & 1) res = res * base % MOD;
        base = base * base % MOD;
        exp >>= 1;
    }
    return res;
}

ll modInv(ll x) {
    return modPow(x, MOD - 2);
}

void add(int& a, int b) {

    if (a < 0) a += MOD;

    ModInt(ll _v) : v(normS(_v % mod + mod)) {}
    explicit operator bool() const { return v != 0; }
    static uint normS(const uint &x) { return (x < mod) ? x : x - mod; }
    static ModInt make(const uint &x) { ModInt m; m.v = x; return m; }
    
    ModInt operator+(const ModInt& b) const { return make(normS(v + b.v)); }
    ModInt operator-(const ModInt& b) const { return make(normS(v + mod - b.v)); }
    ModInt operator-() const { return make(normS(mod - v)); }
    ModInt operator*(const ModInt& b) const { return make((ull)v * b.v % mod); }
    ModInt operator/(const ModInt& b) const { return *this * b.inv(); }
    
    ModInt& operator+=(const ModInt& b) { return *this = *this + b; }
    ModInt& operator-=(const ModInt& b) { return *this = *this - b; }
    ModInt& operator*=(const ModInt& b) { return *this = *this * b; }
    ModInt& operator/=(const ModInt& b) { return *this = *this / b; }
    ModInt& operator++(int) { return *this = *this + 1; }
    ModInt& operator--(int) { return *this = *this - 1; }
    
    ll extgcd(ll a, ll b, ll &x, ll &y) const {
        ll p[]{a, 1, 0}, q[]{b, 0, 1};
        while (*q) {
            ll t = *p / *q;
            for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) swap(p[i] -= t * q[i], q[i]);
        }
        if (p[0] < 0) for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) p[i] = -p[i];
        x = p[1], y = p[2];
        return p[0];
    }
    
    ModInt inv() const {
        ll x, y;
        extgcd(v, mod, x, y);
        return make(normS(x + mod));
    }

            p >>= 1;
        }

#define show(x) cerr << "LINE" << __LINE__ << " : " << #x << " = " << (x) << endl
#else
#define show(x) (void)0

int main() {
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cout << fixed << setprecision(20);

    int N;
    cin >> N;
    vector<vector<mint>> p(N, vector<mint>(N));
    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i)
        for (int j = 0; j < N; ++j) {
            cin >> p[i][j];
            p[i][j] /= 100;
        }

    using BS = bitset<128>;
    unordered_map<BS, mint> cur, nxt;
    {
        BS b;
        b[0] = true;
        cur[b] = 1;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
        for (const auto& kv : cur) {
            BS b = kv.first;
            vector<int> ones;
            for (int idx = 0; idx < N; ++idx)
                if (b[idx]) ones.push_back(idx);
            
            for (int e = 0; e < (1 << N); ++e) {
                mint pr = 1;
                for (int j = 0; j < N; ++j) {
                    if ((e >> j) & 1) pr *= p[i][j];
                    else pr *= mint(1) - p[i][j];
                }
                
                BS nb;
                for (int x : ones) {
                    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r) {
                        if (((e >> r) & 1) && !((x >> r) & 1)) {
                            nb[x | (1 << r)] = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
                nxt[nb] += kv.second * pr;
            }
        }
        cur.swap(nxt);
        nxt.clear();
    }

    mint ans = 0;
    BS full;
    full.set();
    for (const auto& kv : cur)
        if (kv.first[(1 << N) - 1]) ans += kv.second;

problem_description.description: Alice and Bob are playing a game with a string of characters, with Alice going first. The string consists n characters, each of which is one of the first k letters of the alphabet. On a player’s turn, they can either arbitrarily permute the characters in the words, or delete exactly one character in the word (if there is at least one character). In addition, their resulting word cannot have appeared before throughout the entire game. The player unable to make a valid move loses the game.Given n, k, p, find the number of words with exactly n characters consisting of the first k letters of the alphabet such that Alice will win if both Alice and Bob play optimally. Return this number modulo the prime number p.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of input will contain three integers n, k, p (1 ≤ n ≤ 250 000, 1 ≤ k ≤ 26, 108 ≤ p ≤ 109 + 100, p will be prime).
problem_description.output_spec: Print a single integer, the number of winning words for Alice, modulo p.
problem_description.notes: NoteThere are 14 strings that that Alice can win with. For example, some strings are "bbaa" and "baaa". Alice will lose on strings like "aaaa" or "bbbb".

#include <iostream>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

const int MAX_N = 250005;
int n, k, mod;
using ll = long long;

ll modPow(ll base, ll exp) {
    ll res = 1;
    base %= mod;
    while (exp) {
        if (exp & 1) res = (res * base) % mod;
        base = (base * base) % mod;
        exp >>= 1;
    }
    return res;
}

inline int lowbit(int x) { return x & -x; }

ll fact[MAX_N], invFact[MAX_N];
ll memo[26][MAX_N];

ll solve(int pos, int mask) {
    if (memo[pos][mask] != -1) return memo[pos][mask];
    
    if (mask == 0) {
        memo[pos][mask] = fact[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < pos; ++i) {
            memo[pos][mask] = (memo[pos][mask] * (k - i)) % mod;
        }
        return memo[pos][mask];
    }
    
    memo[pos][mask] = 0;
    int rest = mask ^ lowbit(mask);
    
    for (int sub = rest; sub; sub = (sub - 1) & rest) {
        memo[pos][mask] = (memo[pos][mask] + invFact[mask ^ sub] * solve(pos + 1, sub)) % mod;
    }
    
    memo[pos][mask] = (memo[pos][mask] + invFact[mask] * solve(pos + 1, 0)) % mod;
    return memo[pos][mask];
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    
    cin >> n >> k >> mod;
    ll total = modPow(k, n);
    
    if (n & 1) {
        cout << total << '\n';
        return 0;
    }
    
    fact[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) fact[i] = fact[i-1] * i % mod;
    
    invFact[n] = modPow(fact[n], mod - 2);
    for (int i = n; i > 0; --i) invFact[i-1] = invFact[i] * i % mod;
    
    memset(memo, -1, sizeof(memo));
    ll bad = solve(0, n);
    ll ans = (total - bad + mod) % mod;
    cout << ans << '\n';
    
    return 0;
}

using namespace std;

const int MAX_N = 250005;
int n, k, P;
using ll = long long;

ll mod_exp(ll base, ll exp) {
    ll res = 1;
    base %= P;
    while (exp) {
        if (exp & 1) res = (res * base) % P;
        base = (base * base) % P;
        exp >>= 1;
    }
    return res;
}

inline int get_lowest_set_bit(int x) { return x & -x; }

ll factorial[MAX_N], inv_factorial[MAX_N];
ll cache[26][MAX_N];

ll compute(int level, int bits) {
    if (cache[level][bits] != -1) return cache[level][bits];
    
    if (bits == 0) {
        cache[level][bits] = factorial[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < level; ++i) {
            cache[level][bits] = (cache[level][bits] * (k - i)) % P;
        }
        return cache[level][bits];
    }
    
    cache[level][bits] = 0;
    int remaining = bits ^ get_lowest_set_bit(bits);
    
    for (int subset = remaining; subset; subset = (subset - 1) & remaining) {
        cache[level][bits] = (cache[level][bits] + inv_factorial[bits ^ subset] * compute(level + 1, subset)) % P;
    }
    
    cache[level][bits] = (cache[level][bits] + inv_factorial[bits] * compute(level + 1, 0)) % P;
    return cache[level][bits];
}

    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    if (n & 1) {
        cout << total << '\n';
        return 0;
    }
    
    factorial[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) factorial[i] = factorial[i-1] * i % P;
    
    inv_factorial[n] = mod_exp(factorial[n], P - 2);
    for (int i = n; i > 0; --i) inv_factorial[i-1] = inv_factorial[i] * i % P;
    
    memset(cache, -1, sizeof(cache));
    ll invalid = compute(0, n);
    ll result = (total - invalid + P) % P;
    cout << result << '\n';
    
    return 0;
}

#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int n, k, MOD;
int factorial[250003], inv_factorial[250003];
int cache[27][250003];

inline int LSB(int x) { return x & -x; }

int mod_exp(int base, int exponent) {
    int result = 1;
    while (exponent) {
        if (exponent & 1) result = (1LL * result * base) % MOD;
        base = (1LL * base * base) % MOD;
        exponent >>= 1;
    }
    return result;
}

void precompute() {
    factorial[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        factorial[i] = (1LL * factorial[i-1] * i) % MOD;
    inv_factorial[n] = mod_exp(factorial[n], MOD - 2);
    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        inv_factorial[i] = (1LL * inv_factorial[i+1] * (i+1)) % MOD;
}

int compute(int depth, int bitmask) {
    if (cache[depth][bitmask] != -1) return cache[depth][bitmask];
    if (bitmask == 0) {
        cache[depth][bitmask] = (1LL * factorial[n] * factorial[k] % MOD) * inv_factorial[k - depth] % MOD;
        return cache[depth][bitmask];
    }
    int remaining = bitmask - LSB(bitmask);
    cache[depth][bitmask] = 0;
    for (int submask = remaining; submask; submask = (submask - 1) & remaining)
        cache[depth][bitmask] = (cache[depth][bitmask] + 1LL * compute(depth + 1, submask) * inv_factorial[bitmask - submask] % MOD) % MOD;
    cache[depth][bitmask] = (cache[depth][bitmask] + 1LL * compute(depth + 1, 0) * inv_factorial[bitmask] % MOD) % MOD;
    return cache[depth][bitmask];
}

int main() {
    scanf("%d %d %d", &n, &k, &MOD);
    precompute();
    int result = mod_exp(k, n);
    if (n % 2 == 0) {
        memset(cache, -1, sizeof(cache));
        result = (result - compute(0, n) + MOD) % MOD;
    }
    printf("%d", result);
    return 0;
}

#include <iostream>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int N, K, MODULO;
int fact[250003], inv_fact[250003];
int memo[27][250003];

int get_lowest_set_bit(int x) { return x & -x; }

int modular_exponentiation(int base, int power) {
    int res = 1;
    while (power > 0) {
        if (power & 1) res = (1LL * res * base) % MODULO;
        base = (1LL * base * base) % MODULO;
        power >>= 1;
    }
    return res;
}

void build_tables() {
    fact[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i)
        fact[i] = (1LL * fact[i-1] * i) % MODULO;
    inv_fact[N] = modular_exponentiation(fact[N], MODULO - 2);
    for (int i = N - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        inv_fact[i] = (1LL * inv_fact[i+1] * (i+1)) % MODULO;
}

int recursive_solve(int level, int mask) {
    if (memo[level][mask] != -1) return memo[level][mask];
    if (mask == 0) {
        memo[level][mask] = (1LL * fact[N] * fact[K] % MODULO) * inv_fact[K - level] % MODULO;
        return memo[level][mask];
    }
    int rest = mask - get_lowest_set_bit(mask);
    memo[level][mask] = 0;
    for (int sub = rest; sub; sub = (sub - 1) & rest)
        memo[level][mask] = (memo[level][mask] + 1LL * recursive_solve(level + 1, sub) * inv_fact[mask - sub] % MODULO) % MODULO;
    memo[level][mask] = (memo[level][mask] + 1LL * recursive_solve(level + 1, 0) * inv_fact[mask] % MODULO) % MODULO;
    return memo[level][mask];
}

int main() {
    scanf("%d %d %d", &N, &K, &MODULO);
    build_tables();
    int answer = modular_exponentiation(K, N);
    if (N % 2 == 0) {
        memset(memo, -1, sizeof(memo));
        answer = (answer - recursive_solve(0, N) + MODULO) % MODULO;
    }
    printf("%d", answer);
    return 0;
}

#include <iostream>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int N, K, MOD;
int factorial[250003], inv_factorial[250003];
int dp_table[27][250003];

inline int extract_lowest_bit(int x) { return x & -x; }

int fast_power(int b, int e) {
    int res = 1;
    while (e) {
        if (e & 1) res = (1LL * res * b) % MOD;
        b = (1LL * b * b) % MOD;
        e >>= 1;
    }
    return res;
}

void prepare() {
    factorial[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i)
        factorial[i] = (1LL * factorial[i-1] * i) % MOD;
    inv_factorial[N] = fast_power(factorial[N], MOD - 2);
    for (int i = N - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        inv_factorial[i] = (1LL * inv_factorial[i+1] * (i+1)) % MOD;
}

int solve(int depth, int bits) {
    if (dp_table[depth][bits] != -1) return dp_table[depth][bits];
    if (bits == 0) {
        dp_table[depth][bits] = (1LL * factorial[N] * factorial[K] % MOD) * inv_factorial[K - depth] % MOD;
        return dp_table[depth][bits];
    }
    int remainder = bits - extract_lowest_bit(bits);
    dp_table[depth][bits] = 0;
    for (int subset = remainder; subset; subset = (subset - 1) & remainder)
        dp_table[depth][bits] = (dp_table[depth][bits] + 1LL * solve(depth + 1, subset) * inv_factorial[bits - subset] % MOD) % MOD;
    dp_table[depth][bits] = (dp_table[depth][bits] + 1LL * solve(depth + 1, 0) * inv_factorial[bits] % MOD) % MOD;
    return dp_table[depth][bits];
}

int main() {
    scanf("%d %d %d", &N, &K, &MOD);
    prepare();
    int total = fast_power(K, N);
    if (N % 2 == 0) {
        memset(dp_table, -1, sizeof(dp_table));
        total = (total - solve(0, N) + MOD) % MOD;
    }
    printf("%d", total);
    return 0;
}

#include <cstring>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int N, K, M;
int fact[250003], inv_fact[250003];
int memo[27][250003];

int get_lsb(int x) { return x & -x; }

int mod_pow(int b, int e) {
    int r = 1;
    while (e) {
        if (e & 1) r = (1LL * r * b) % M;
        b = (1LL * b * b) % M;
        e >>= 1;
    }
    return r;
}

void init_tables() {
    fact[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i)
        fact[i] = (1LL * fact[i-1] * i) % M;
    inv_fact[N] = mod_pow(fact[N], M - 2);
    for (int i = N - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        inv_fact[i] = (1LL * inv_fact[i+1] * (i+1)) % M;
}

int f(int lvl, int mask) {
    if (memo[lvl][mask] != -1) return memo[lvl][mask];
    if (mask == 0) {
        memo[lvl][mask] = (1LL * fact[N] * fact[K] % M) * inv_fact[K - lvl] % M;
        return memo[lvl][mask];
    }
    int rem = mask - get_lsb(mask);
    memo[lvl][mask] = 0;
    for (int sub = rem; sub; sub = (sub - 1) & rem)
        memo[lvl][mask] = (memo[lvl][mask] + 1LL * f(lvl + 1, sub) * inv_fact[mask - sub] % M) % M;
    memo[lvl][mask] = (memo[lvl][mask] + 1LL * f(lvl + 1, 0) * inv_fact[mask] % M) % M;
    return memo[lvl][mask];
}

int main() {
    scanf("%d %d %d", &N, &K, &M);
    init_tables();
    int res = mod_pow(K, N);
    if (N % 2 == 0) {
        memset(memo, -1, sizeof(memo));
        res = (res - f(0, N) + M) % M;
    }
    printf("%d", res);
    return 0;
}

problem_description.description: Today is the final contest of INOI (Iranian National Olympiad in Informatics). The contest room is a row with $$$n$$$ computers. All computers are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. There are $$$m$$$ participants, numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$.We have an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$m$$$ where $$$a_{i}$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) is the computer behind which the $$$i$$$-th participant wants to sit.Also, we have another array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ consisting of characters 'L' and 'R'. $$$b_i$$$ is the side from which the $$$i$$$-th participant enters the room. 'L' means the participant enters from the left of computer $$$1$$$ and goes from left to right, and 'R' means the participant enters from the right of computer $$$n$$$ and goes from right to left.The participants in the order from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ enter the room one by one. The $$$i$$$-th of them enters the contest room in the direction $$$b_i$$$ and goes to sit behind the $$$a_i$$$-th computer. If it is occupied he keeps walking in his direction until he reaches the first unoccupied computer. After that, he sits behind it. If he doesn't find any computer he gets upset and gives up on the contest.The madness of the $$$i$$$-th participant is the distance between his assigned computer ($$$a_i$$$) and the computer he ends up sitting behind. The distance between computers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ is equal to $$$|i - j|$$$.The values in the array $$$a$$$ can be equal. There exist $$$n^m \cdot 2^m$$$ possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$.Consider all pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$ such that no person becomes upset. For each of them let's calculate the sum of participants madnesses. Find the sum of all these values.You will be given some prime modulo $$$p$$$. Find this sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$p$$$ ($$$1 \leq m \leq n \leq 500, 10^8 \leq p \leq 10 ^ 9 + 9$$$). It is guaranteed, that the number $$$p$$$ is prime.
problem_description.output_spec: Print only one integer — the required sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test, there are three possible arrays $$$a$$$: $$$\{1\}$$$, $$$\{2\}$$$, and $$$ \{3\}$$$ and two possible arrays $$$b$$$: $$$\{\mathtt{L}\}$$$ and $$$\{\mathtt{R}\}$$$. For all six pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, the only participant will sit behind the computer $$$a_1$$$, so his madness will be $$$0$$$. All computers are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. If he doesn't find any computer he gets upset and gives up on the contest.The madness of the $$$i$$$-th participant is the distance between his assigned computer ($$$a_i$$$) and the computer he ends up sitting behind. constexpr int inf = 0x3f3f3f3f;
constexpr int maxn = 510;
int mod;

int fat[maxn], inv[maxn], inv_fat[maxn];

void calc() {
	fat[0] = fat[1] = inv[1] = inv_fat[0] = inv_fat[1] = 1;
	for(int i = 2; i < maxn; i++) {
		fat[i] = (int)(1ll * fat[i-1] * i % mod);
		inv[i] = mod - (int)(1ll * (mod/i) * inv[mod%i] % mod);
		inv_fat[i] = (int)(1ll * inv_fat[i-1] * inv[i] % mod);
	}
}

inline int choose(int a, int b) {
	return (int)(1ll * fat[a] * (1ll * inv_fat[b] * inv_fat[a-b] % mod) % mod);
}

inline ll p(int x) { return 1ll * x * (x+1) / 2; }

int f[maxn], c[maxn], dp1[maxn][maxn], dp2[maxn][maxn];

int main() {
	int n, m; scanf("%d %d %d", &n, &m, &mod);
	calc();
	f[0] = 1;
	for(int i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
		for(int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
			f[i] = (f[i] + (int)((1ll * choose(i-1, j) * f[j] % mod) * f[i-1-j] % mod)) % mod;
			c[i] = (c[i] + (int)((1ll * (i+1) * choose(i-1, j) % mod) *
				((1ll * f[j] * c[i-1-j] % mod) + (1ll * f[i-1-j] * c[j] % mod) % mod) % mod)) % mod;
			c[i] = (c[i] + (int)((1ll * choose(i-1, j) * (p(j) + p(i-1-j)) % mod) *
				(1ll * f[j] * f[i-1-j] % mod) % mod)) % mod;
		}
		f[i] = (int)(1ll * f[i] * (i+1) % mod);
	}
	dp1[0][0] = 1;
	for(int k = 1; k <= n; k++) {
		dp1[k][0] = 1;
		for(int i = 1; i <= min(m, k); i++) {
			dp1[k][i] = dp1[k-1][i];
			dp2[k][i] = dp2[k-1][i];
			for(int j = 1; j <= i; j++) {
				dp1[k][i] = (dp1[k][i] + (int)((1ll * f[j] * dp1[max(k-j-1, 0)][i-j] % mod) * choose(i, j) % mod)) % mod;
				dp2[k][i] = (dp2[k][i] + (int)((1ll * c[j] * dp1[max(k-j-1, 0)][i-j] % mod) * choose(i, j) % mod)) % mod;
				dp2[k][i] = (dp2[k][i] + (int)((1ll * f[j] * dp2[max(k-j-1, 0)][i-j] % mod) * choose(i, j) % mod)) % mod;
			}
		}
	}
	printf("%d\n", dp2[n][m]);
}

problem_description.description: Today is the final contest of INOI (Iranian National Olympiad in Informatics). The contest room is a row with $$$n$$$ computers. All computers are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. There are $$$m$$$ participants, numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$.We have an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$m$$$ where $$$a_{i}$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) is the computer behind which the $$$i$$$-th participant wants to sit.Also, we have another array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ consisting of characters 'L' and 'R'. $$$b_i$$$ is the side from which the $$$i$$$-th participant enters the room. 'L' means the participant enters from the left of computer $$$1$$$ and goes from left to right, and 'R' means the participant enters from the right of computer $$$n$$$ and goes from right to left.The participants in the order from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ enter the room one by one. The $$$i$$$-th of them enters the contest room in the direction $$$b_i$$$ and goes to sit behind the $$$a_i$$$-th computer. If it is occupied he keeps walking in his direction until he reaches the first unoccupied computer. After that, he sits behind it. If he doesn't find any computer he gets upset and gives up on the contest.The madness of the $$$i$$$-th participant is the distance between his assigned computer ($$$a_i$$$) and the computer he ends up sitting behind. The distance between computers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ is equal to $$$|i - j|$$$.The values in the array $$$a$$$ can be equal. There exist $$$n^m \cdot 2^m$$$ possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$.Consider all pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$ such that no person becomes upset. For each of them let's calculate the sum of participants madnesses. Find the sum of all these values.You will be given some prime modulo $$$p$$$. Find this sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$p$$$ ($$$1 \leq m \leq n \leq 500, 10^8 \leq p \leq 10 ^ 9 + 9$$$). It is guaranteed, that the number $$$p$$$ is prime.
problem_description.output_spec: Print only one integer — the required sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test, there are three possible arrays $$$a$$$: $$$\{1\}$$$, $$$\{2\}$$$, and $$$ \{3\}$$$ and two possible arrays $$$b$$$: $$$\{\mathtt{L}\}$$$ and $$$\{\mathtt{R}\}$$$. For all six pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, the only participant will sit behind the computer $$$a_1$$$, so his madness will be $$$0$$$. So the total sum of madnesses will be $$$0$$$.In the second test, all possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, such that no person becomes upset are:  $$$(\{1, 1\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{L}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{1, 1\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{L}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{2, 2\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{R}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{2, 2\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{R}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  all possible pairs of $$$a \in \{\{1, 2\}, \{2, 1\}\}$$$ and $$$b \in \{\{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{L}\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{L}\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{R}\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{R}\}\}$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$0$$$. So, the answer is $$$1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 \ldots = 4$$$.

problem_description.description: Today is the final contest of INOI (Iranian National Olympiad in Informatics). The contest room is a row with $$$n$$$ computers. All computers are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. There are $$$m$$$ participants, numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$.We have an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$m$$$ where $$$a_{i}$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) is the computer behind which the $$$i$$$-th participant wants to sit.Also, we have another array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ consisting of characters 'L' and 'R'. $$$b_i$$$ is the side from which the $$$i$$$-th participant enters the room. 'L' means the participant enters from the left of computer $$$1$$$ and goes from left to right, and 'R' means the participant enters from the right of computer $$$n$$$ and goes from right to left.The participants in the order from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ enter the room one by one. The $$$i$$$-th of them enters the contest room in the direction $$$b_i$$$ and goes to sit behind the $$$a_i$$$-th computer. If it is occupied he keeps walking in his direction until he reaches the first unoccupied computer. After that, he sits behind it. If he doesn't find any computer he gets upset and gives up on the contest.The madness of the $$$i$$$-th participant is the distance between his assigned computer ($$$a_i$$$) and the computer he ends up sitting behind. The distance between computers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ is equal to $$$|i - j|$$$.The values in the array $$$a$$$ can be equal. There exist $$$n^m \cdot 2^m$$$ possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$.Consider all pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$ such that no person becomes upset. For each of them let's calculate the sum of participants madnesses. Find the sum of all these values.You will be given some prime modulo $$$p$$$. Find this sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$p$$$ ($$$1 \leq m \leq n \leq 500, 10^8 \leq p \leq 10 ^ 9 + 9$$$). It is guaranteed, that the number $$$p$$$ is prime.
problem_description.output_spec: Print only one integer — the required sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test, there are three possible arrays $$$a$$$: $$$\{1\}$$$, $$$\{2\}$$$, and $$$ \{3\}$$$ and two possible arrays $$$b$$$: $$$\{\mathtt{L}\}$$$ and $$$\{\mathtt{R}\}$$$. For all six pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, the only participant will sit behind the computer $$$a_1$$$, so his madness will be $$$0$$$. So the total sum of madnesses will be $$$0$$$.In the second test, all possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, such that no person becomes upset are:  $$$(\{1, 1\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{L}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{1, 1\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{L}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{2, 2\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{R}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{2, 2\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{R}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  all possible pairs of $$$a \in \{\{1, 2\}, \{2, 1\}\}$$$ and $$$b \in \{\{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{L}\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{L}\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{R}\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{R}\}\}$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$0$$$. So, the answer is $$$1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 \ldots = 4$$$.

All computers are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. There are $$$m$$$ participants, numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$.We have an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$m$$$ where $$$a_{i}$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) is the computer behind which the $$$i$$$-th participant wants to sit.Also, we have another array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ consisting of characters 'L' and 'R'. $$$b_i$$$ is the side from which the $$$i$$$-th participant enters the room. 'L' means the participant enters from the left of computer $$$1$$$ and goes from left to right, and 'R' means the participant enters from the right of computer $$$n$$$ and goes from right to left.The participants in the order from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ enter the room one by one. The $$$i$$$-th of them enters the contest room in the direction $$$b_i$$$ and goes to sit behind the $$$a_i$$$-th computer. If it is occupied he keeps walking in his direction until he reaches the first unoccupied computer. After that, he sits behind it. If he doesn't find any computer he gets upset and gives up on the contest.The madness of the $$$i$$$-th participant is the distance between his assigned computer ($$$a_i$$$) and the computer he ends up sitting behind. The distance between computers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ is equal to $$$|i - j|$$$.The values in the array $$$a$$$ can be equal. There exist $$$n^m \cdot 2^m$$$ possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$.Consider all pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$ such that no person becomes upset. For each of them let's calculate the sum of participants madnesses. Find the sum of all these values.You will be given some prime modulo $$$p$$$. Find this sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$p$$$ ($$$1 \leq m \leq n \leq 500, 10^8 \leq p \leq 10 ^ 9 + 9$$$). It is guaranteed, that the number $$$p$$$ is prime.
problem_description.output_spec: Print only one integer — the required sum by modulo $$$p$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test, there are three possible arrays $$$a$$$: $$$\{1\}$$$, $$$\{2\}$$$, and $$$ \{3\}$$$ and two possible arrays $$$b$$$: $$$\{\mathtt{L}\}$$$ and $$$\{\mathtt{R}\}$$$. For all six pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, the only participant will sit behind the computer $$$a_1$$$, so his madness will be $$$0$$$. So the total sum of madnesses will be $$$0$$$.In the second test, all possible pairs of arrays $$$(a, b)$$$, such that no person becomes upset are:  $$$(\{1, 1\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{L}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{1, 1\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{L}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{2, 2\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{R}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  $$$(\{2, 2\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{R}\})$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$1$$$;  all possible pairs of $$$a \in \{\{1, 2\}, \{2, 1\}\}$$$ and $$$b \in \{\{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{L}\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{L}\}, \{\mathtt{L}, \mathtt{R}\}, \{\mathtt{R}, \mathtt{R}\}\}$$$, the sum of madnesses is $$$0$$$. So, the answer is $$$1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 \ldots = 4$$$.

All computers are numbered with integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. If he doesn't find any computer he gets upset and gives up on the contest.The madness of the $$$i$$$-th participant is the distance between his assigned computer ($$$a_i$$$) and the computer he ends up sitting behind. problem_description.description: The game of Egg Roulette is played between two players. Initially 2R raw eggs and 2C cooked eggs are placed randomly into a carton. The shells are left on so there is no way to distinguish a raw egg from a cooked egg. One at a time, a player will select an egg, and then smash the egg on his/her forehead. If the egg was cooked, not much happens, but if the egg was raw, it will make quite the mess. This continues until one player has broken R raw eggs, at which point that player is declared the loser and the other player wins.The order in which players take turns can be described as a string of 'A' and 'B' characters, where the i-th character tells which player should choose the i-th egg. Traditionally, players take turns going one after the other. That is, they follow the ordering "ABABAB...". This isn't very fair though, because the second player will win more often than the first. We'd like you to find a better ordering for the players to take their turns. Let's define the unfairness of an ordering as the absolute difference between the first player's win probability and the second player's win probability. We're interested in orderings that minimize the unfairness. We only consider an ordering valid if it contains the same number of 'A's as 'B's.You will also be given a string S of length 2(R + C) containing only 'A', 'B', and '?' characters. An ordering is said to match S if it only differs from S in positions where S contains a '?'. Of the valid orderings that minimize unfairness, how many match S?
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of input will contain integers R and C (1 ≤ R, C ≤ 20, R + C ≤ 30). The second line of input will contain the string S of length 2(R + C) consisting only of characters 'A', 'B', '?'.
problem_description.output_spec: Print the number of valid orderings that minimize unfairness and match S.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test case, the minimum unfairness is 0, and the orderings that achieve it are "ABBA" and "BAAB", neither of which match S. Note that an ordering such as "ABBB" would also have an unfairness of 0, but is invalid because it does not contain the same number of 'A's as 'B's.In the second example, the only matching ordering is "BBAAABABABBA".

#include <iostream>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>

using namespace std;

typedef long long ll;
const int MAX_SIZE = 66;

int rows, cols, total_len, loop_idx;
char buffer[MAX_SIZE];
ll C[MAX_SIZE][MAX_SIZE];

int cntA[MAX_SIZE], cntB[MAX_SIZE];
vector<ll> partA[MAX_SIZE], partB[MAX_SIZE];

void init_binom() {
    for (int i = 0; i <= total_len; ++i) {
        C[i][0] = 1;
        for (int j = 1; j <= i; ++j)
            C[i][j] = C[i-1][j-1] + C[i-1][j];
    }
}

ll diff_calc(int pattern, int a_cnt, int b_cnt) {
    ll res = 0;
    ll t1, t2;

    for (int k = 0; k < cols + 1; ++k) {
        if (pattern & (1 << k)) {
            ++b_cnt;
            t1 = C[b_cnt - 1][rows - 1];
            t2 = C[total_len - b_cnt][rows] - C[a_cnt][rows];
            res -= t1 * t2;
        } else {
            ++a_cnt;
            t1 = C[a_cnt - 1][rows - 1];
            t2 = C[total_len - a_cnt][rows] - C[b_cnt][rows];
            res += t1 * t2;
        }
    }
    return res;
}

bool is_valid(int pattern) {
    for (int k = 0; k < cols + 1; ++k) {
        if (buffer[2 * rows + cols + k] == 'A' && ((pattern >> k) & 1) == 1) return false;
        if (buffer[2 * rows + cols + k] == 'B' && ((pattern >> k) & 1) == 0) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void build_tables() {
    int max_pat = 1 << (cols + 1);

    for (int pat = 0; pat < max_pat; ++pat) {
        int b_here = __builtin_popcount(pat);
        int a_here = cols + 1 - b_here;

        if (is_valid(pat))
            partA[a_here].push_back(diff_calc(pat, rows + cols - a_here, rows + cols - b_here));
        else
            partB[a_here].push_back(diff_calc(pat, rows + cols - a_here, rows + cols - b_here));
    }

    for (int i = 0; i <= cols + 1; ++i) {
        sort(partA[i].begin(), partA[i].end());
        sort(partB[i].begin(), partB[i].end());
    }
}

ll get_coeff(int pattern) {
    int i, j;

    for (i = 0; i < cols + 1; ++i)
        if (((pattern >> i) & 1) != (pattern & 1))
            break;

    for (j = i; j < cols + 1; ++j) {
        if (buffer[2 * rows - 1 + j] == 'A' && (((pattern >> j) & 1) == 1)) return 0;
        if (buffer[2 * rows - 1 + j] == 'B' && (((pattern >> j) & 1) == 0)) return 0;
    }

    int set_a = rows - 1 + ((pattern & 1) == 0 ? i : 0);
    int set_b = rows - 1 + ((pattern & 1) == 1 ? i : 0);

    if (set_a < cntA[2 * rows - 2 + i]) return 0;
    if (set_b < cntB[2 * rows - 2 + i]) return 0;
    return C[set_a + set_b - cntA[2 * rows - 2 + i] - cntB[2 * rows - 2 + i]][set_a - cntA[2 * rows - 2 + i]];
}

void update_min(pair<ll, ll>& best, pair<ll, ll> cand) {
    if (cand.first < 0) cand.first = -cand.first;

    if (best.first < cand.first) return;
    if (best.first > cand.first) {
        best = cand;
        return;
    }
    best.second += cand.second;
}

ll count_equal(const vector<ll>& vec, ll val) {
    auto lb = lower_bound(vec.begin(), vec.end(), val);
    auto ub = upper_bound(vec.begin(), vec.end(), val);
    return ub - lb;
}

ll solve_first() {
    int max_pat = 1 << (cols + 1);
    pair<ll, ll> best = make_pair(1LL << 60, 0);

    for (int pat = 0; pat < max_pat; ++pat) {
        int b_here = __builtin_popcount(pat);
        int a_here = cols + 1 - b_here;
        ll cur_val = diff_calc(pat, rows - 1, rows - 1);

        ll coeff = get_coeff(pat);
        auto it = lower_bound(partA[cols + 1 - a_here].begin(), partA[cols + 1 - a_here].end(), -cur_val);

        if (it != partA[cols + 1 - a_here].end()) {
            if (best.first >= abs(*it + cur_val)) {
                ll c2 = count_equal(partA[cols + 1 - a_here], *it);
                update_min(best, make_pair(*it + cur_val, coeff * c2));
            }
        }

        if (it != partA[cols + 1 - a_here].begin()) {
            --it;
            if (best.first >= abs(*it + cur_val)) {
                ll c2 = count_equal(partA[cols + 1 - a_here], *it);
                update_min(best, make_pair(*it + cur_val, coeff * c2));
            }
        }

        coeff = 0;
        it = lower_bound(partB[cols + 1 - a_here].begin(), partB[cols + 1 - a_here].end(), -cur_val);

        if (it != partB[cols + 1 - a_here].end()) {
            ll c2 = count_equal(partB[cols + 1 - a_here], *it);
            if (best.first >= abs(*it + cur_val)) {
                update_min(best, make_pair(*it + cur_val, coeff * c2));
            }
        }

        if (it != partB[cols + 1 - a_here].begin()) {
            --it;
            if (best.first >= abs(*it + cur_val)) {
                ll c2 = count_equal(partB[cols + 1 - a_here], *it);
                update_min(best, make_pair(*it + cur_val, coeff * c2));
            }
        }
    }

    return best.second;
}

int main() {
    scanf("%d%d\n%s", &rows, &cols, buffer + 1);
    total_len = 2 * (rows + cols);

    init_binom();

    for (loop_idx = 1; loop_idx <= total_len; ++loop_idx) {
        cntA[loop_idx] = cntA[loop_idx - 1] + (buffer[loop_idx] == 'A' ? 1 : 0);
        cntB[loop_idx] = cntB[loop_idx - 1] + (buffer[loop_idx] == 'B' ? 1 : 0);
    }

    build_tables();
    ll answer = solve_first();
    printf("%lld", answer);

    return 0;
}

#include <iostream>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>

using namespace std;

using llong = long long;
constexpr int MAX_LEN = 66;

int R, C, N, loop_var;
char str[MAX_LEN];
llong binomial[MAX_LEN][MAX_LEN];

int cntA[MAX_LEN], cntB[MAX_LEN];
vector<llong> vec_part[MAX_LEN], vec_zero[MAX_LEN];

void build_binomial_table() {
    for (int i = 0; i <= N; ++i) {
        binomial[i][0] = 1;
        for (int j = 1; j <= i; ++j)
            binomial[i][j] = binomial[i-1][j-1] + binomial[i-1][j];
    }
}

llong compute_diff(int config, int a_prev, int b_prev) {
    llong total = 0;
    llong t1, t2;

    for (int k = 0; k < C + 1; ++k) {
        if (config & (1 << k)) {
            ++b_prev;
            t1 = binomial[b_prev - 1][R - 1];
            t2 = binomial[N - b_prev][R] - binomial[a_prev][R];
            total -= t1 * t2;
        } else {
            ++a_prev;
            t1 = binomial[a_prev - 1][R - 1];
            t2 = binomial[N - a_prev][R] - binomial[b_prev][R];
            total += t1 * t2;
        }
    }
    return total;
}

bool config_ok(int config) {
    for (int k = 0; k < C + 1; ++k) {
        if (str[2 * R + C + k] == 'A' && ((config >> k) & 1) == 1) return false;
        if (str[2 * R + C + k] == 'B' && ((config >> k) & 1) == 0) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void prepare_tables() {
    int max_config = 1 << (C + 1);

    for (int cfg = 0; cfg < max_config; ++cfg) {
        int b_here = __builtin_popcount(cfg);
        int a_here = C + 1 - b_here;

        if (config_ok(cfg))
            vec_part[a_here].push_back(compute_diff(cfg, R + C - a_here, R + C - b_here));
        else
            vec_zero[a_here].push_back(compute_diff(cfg, R + C - a_here, R + C - b_here));
    }

    for (int i = 0; i <= C + 1; ++i) {
        sort(vec_part[i].begin(), vec_part[i].end());
        sort(vec_zero[i].begin(), vec_zero[i].end());
    }
}

llong get_factor(int config) {
    int i, j;

    for (i = 0; i < C + 1; ++i)
        if (((config >> i) & 1) != (config & 1))
            break;

    for (j = i; j < C + 1; ++j) {
        if (str[2 * R - 1 + j] == 'A' && (((config >> j) & 1) == 1)) return 0;
        if (str[2 * R - 1 + j] == 'B' && (((config >> j) & 1) == 0)) return 0;
    }

    int set_a = R - 1 + ((config & 1) == 0 ? i : 0);
    int set_b = R - 1 + ((config & 1) == 1 ? i : 0);

    if (set_a < cntA[2 * R - 2 + i]) return 0;
    if (set_b < cntB[2 * R - 2 + i]) return 0;
    return binomial[set_a + set_b - cntA[2 * R - 2 + i] - cntB[2 * R - 2 + i]][set_a - cntA[2 * R - 2 + i]];
}

void update_best(pair<llong, llong>& best, pair<llong, llong> candidate) {
    if (candidate.first < 0) candidate.first = -candidate.first;

    if (best.first < candidate.first) return;
    if (best.first > candidate.first) {
        best = candidate;
        return;
    }
    best.second += candidate.second;
}

llong count_occurrences(const vector<llong>& arr, llong target) {
    auto lo = lower_bound(arr.begin(), arr.end(), target);
    auto hi = upper_bound(arr.begin(), arr.end(), target);
    return hi - lo;
}

llong compute_solution() {
    int max_config = 1 << (C + 1);
    pair<llong, llong> best = make_pair(1LL << 60, 0);

    for (int cfg = 0; cfg < max_config; ++cfg) {
        int b_here = __builtin_popcount(cfg);

        if (iter != vec_part[C + 1 - a_here].end()) {
            if (best.first >= abs(*iter + current)) {
                llong factor2 = count_occurrences(vec_part[C + 1 - a_here], *iter);
                update_best(best, make_pair(*iter + current, factor * factor2));
            }
        }

        if (iter != vec_part[C + 1 - a_here].begin()) {
            --iter;
            if (best.first >= abs(*iter + current)) {
                llong factor2 = count_occurrences(vec_part[C + 1 - a_here], *iter);
                update_best(best, make_pair(*iter + current, factor * factor2));
            }
        }

        factor = 0;
        iter = lower_bound(vec_zero[C + 1 - a_here].begin(), vec_zero[C + 1 - a_here].end(), -current);

        if (iter != vec_zero[C + 1 - a_here].end()) {
            llong factor2 = count_occurrences(vec_zero[C + 1 - a_here], *iter);
            if (best.first >= abs(*iter + current)) {
                update_best(best, make_pair(*iter + current, factor * factor2));
            }
        }

        if (iter != vec_zero[C + 1 - a_here].begin()) {
            --iter;
            if (best.first >= abs(*iter + current)) {
                llong factor2 = count_occurrences(vec_zero[C + 1 - a_here], *iter);
                update_best(best, make_pair(*iter + current, factor * factor2));
            }
        }
    }

    return best.second;
}

    scanf("%d%d\n%s", &R, &C, str + 1);
    N = 2 * (R + C);

    build_binomial_table();

    for (loop_var = 1; loop_var <= N; ++loop_var) {

}

problem_description.description: The game of Egg Roulette is played between two players. Initially 2R raw eggs and 2C cooked eggs are placed randomly into a carton. The shells are left on so there is no way to distinguish a raw egg from a cooked egg. One at a time, a player will select an egg, and then smash the egg on his/her forehead. If the egg was cooked, not much happens, but if the egg was raw, it will make quite the mess. This continues until one player has broken R raw eggs, at which point that player is declared the loser and the other player wins.The order in which players take turns can be described as a string of 'A' and 'B' characters, where the i-th character tells which player should choose the i-th egg. Traditionally, players take turns going one after the other. That is, they follow the ordering "ABABAB...". This isn't very fair though, because the second player will win more often than the first. We'd like you to find a better ordering for the players to take their turns. Let's define the unfairness of an ordering as the absolute difference between the first player's win probability and the second player's win probability. We're interested in orderings that minimize the unfairness. We only consider an ordering valid if it contains the same number of 'A's as 'B's.You will also be given a string S of length 2(R + C) containing only 'A', 'B', and '?' characters. An ordering is said to match S if it only differs from S in positions where S contains a '?'. Of the valid orderings that minimize unfairness, how many match S?
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of input will contain integers R and C (1 ≤ R, C ≤ 20, R + C ≤ 30). The second line of input will contain the string S of length 2(R + C) consisting only of characters 'A', 'B', '?'.
problem_description.output_spec: Print the number of valid orderings that minimize unfairness and match S.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test case, the minimum unfairness is 0, and the orderings that achieve it are "ABBA" and "BAAB", neither of which match S. Note that an ordering such as "ABBB" would also have an unfairness of 0, but is invalid because it does not contain the same number of 'A's as 'B's.In the second example, the only matching ordering is "BBAAABABABBA".
